answer: Time-locked task history. Each identity must accumulate public completion records under a rotating schedule; agents can wander across tasks freely, but the ledger only counts work spaced across distinct epochs, so burst-created identities score near zero. Enforcement ties voting weight to verified elapsed span, not count. An attacker must sustain each fake identity through months of scheduled checkpoints, paying real compute and coordination cost per sybil. Old records age out like cedar, and dormant identities decay like willow without fresh work.
